newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGIP stock jumps at open, Valeo slides.
newsitem.headline: CGIP stock jumps at open, Valeo slides.

text.p: Shares in French holding company CGIP opened 5.4 percent higher at the opening on the Paris bourse while those of car parts maker Valeo, in which it is buying a 20 percent stake, opened 5.05 percent down.
CGIP announced before the open that it was buying 20 percent of Valeo from Cerus, whose stock was 2.26 percent down at 0807 GMT, seven minutes after the start of bourse trading.
At 0809 GMT, CGIP stock was up 3.93 percent at 1190 francs, while the Valeo stock was down 3.67 percent at 299.4 francs.

Cerus, the holding company belonging to Italian financier Carlo de Benedetti, said earlier it was selling its 28 percent stake for 6.5 billion francs, with a possibility of a further 0.2 billion francs, to CGIP, French state bank CDC, and to JP Morgan and GT Corporation.
